title: reading notes: kv-cache & adaptive batching (ICLR 2025 takeaways)
content:
Quick top-line: went through several ICLR '25 papers + talks that are directly relevant to Redwood's runtime improvements: smarter KV cache eviction, adaptive batching with workload-aware latency SLOs, and hybrid quantization profiles. Notes below are informal — action items at the end.

Motivation / context:
- We keep seeing tail latency and cost tradeoffs when supporting mixed sequence lengths and chat workloads. Cache hit patterns are bursty (many short-context requests, some long-context generative flows).
- Two levers matter most for unit economics: reducing repeated token compute (KV cache reuse) and increasing GPU utilization without violating p90/p99 SLOs (adaptive batching).

Key papers + takeaways:
1) "Dynamic KV Cache Eviction for Long Contexts" (arXiv:2409.01234)
   - Idea: fine-grained cache eviction policies based on per-token access recency + per-request importance score. Not just LRU; uses lightweight learned predictor (binary) to mark tokens likely to be reused.
   - Implementation note: predictor is cheap (~vector dot) and can run on CPU thread before enqueuing to GPU. Helps reduce memory pressure on multi-tenant hosts.
   - Relevance: could plug into Dedicated hosts to reduce memory spills and keep larger effective context per GPU.

2) "Workload-aware Adaptive Batching" (ICLR talk)
   - Adaptive batch sizing using predicted remaining generation length + SLO headroom. If predicted tail is short, can wait a bit to form bigger batch.
   - Key engineering piece: very low-overhead length predictor and a batch scheduler that is latency-aware (different weights for p50/p95/SLO).
   - Tradeoffs: slightly increased p50 to reduce cost; configurable per-customer SLO preferred.

3) "Hybrid Quantization for Mixed Precision Inference"
   - Mixed int8/4 and FP16 paths chosen per-layer based on sensitivity. Paper provides cheap per-layer cal metric on a small calibration set.
   - For us: integrate into Optimize suggestions — provide per-model recommended profile with expected quality delta and token-speedup percent.

Practical experiments to run (small->pilot):
- KV predictor ablation: implement a tiny predictor that uses last-usage-window (8 requests) vector and test hit-rate improvement on internal chat traces (ticket: GH #987). Metric: cache hit-rate, memory usage, and p99 latency.
- Adaptive batching simulator: off-line simulate scheduling policy on historical request traces (hosted API) to quantify cost vs p95/p99 impact. Start with per-customer SLO buckets (best-effort, standard, low-latency).
- Hybrid quant profiles: pick two open models we run (redwood-7b-ish & an LLaMA variant), run calibration on small eval corpus and validate generation quality (BLEU/embedding-sim) vs throughput on our infra.

Operational considerations:
- Rollout: feature flags + canary on Dedicated only initially. We need rollout policies to auto-fallback to current behavior if p99 increases beyond threshold.
- Telemetry: add per-request tags for predictor decisions and batch decisions; add synthetic load tests to ensure scheduler doesn't regress under bursty traffic.
- Config surface: expose a few knobs for customers (aggressiveness, target p95). Default: conservative to prioritize latency.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Predictor training: online vs offline? Start offline with periodic retrain. What privacy implications? (no PII; use request metadata only).
- Multi-tenant memory fairness: how does predictor interact with fair share? Might need global admission control.
- Cost accounting: show per-customer estimated $/k token delta if they enable the features (needed for sales + docs).

Action items (who/when):
- Implement KV predictor prototype in serving-runtime branch (assign: Raja) — target: perf bench by 2025-03-03.
- Run adaptive-batching simulation on last 30 days of hosted traces (assign: me/Emma) — due 2025-02-28.
- Add telemetry schema for batch decisions + predictor outputs (assign: Oliver) — due 2025-02-24.

Notes to self:
- Link to paper saved above. Check related ICLR talk recording for scheduler pseudocode.
- Keep experiments small and measurable: define 3 clear metrics (cost per 1M tokens, p95 latency, cache hit-rate).

References:
- arXiv:2409.01234 (dynamic kv cache)
- internal GH PR: redwood-inference/serving-runtime#987 (prototype scheduler)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-1234 (inference optimizations backlog)

End of notes. Will iterate once I have sims + bench data.
